rules.quote: Singular pronouns have a gender-neutral form. Use the forms:
rules.violation_condition: gendered pronouns ('he', 'she', 'him', 'her', 'his', 'hers') used to refer to a gender-neutral singular subject
rules.why: G-2: The specific pronoun replacements are grouped under the main instruction to use gender-neutral forms for singular pronouns.

rules.quote: When the singular ‘they’ is used in a sentence as a gender-neutral term, it takes the plural form of a verb.
rules.violation_condition: a singular verb form used with the gender-neutral singular pronoun 'they'
rules.why: The sentence clearly states a mandatory grammatical requirement for the singular 'they'.

rules.quote: Use the correct case when writing pronouns. Check whether the pronoun should be in the subjective or the objective case – whether it is the subject or object.
rules.violation_condition: a pronoun in the objective case used as a subject, or a pronoun in the subjective case used as an object
rules.why: Core rule dictating proper use of subjective and objective pronoun cases.

covers.quote: Sentences can have reflexive pronouns when the subject is also the object of the verb.

parts.quote: I emailed myself.
The manager emailed myself.

examples.note: Stripped trailing bracketed gloss following policy E-1.

parts.quote: The manager emailed themself.

rules.quote: Don’t use a reflexive pronoun if the subject and the object are not the same person or thing.
rules.violation_condition: a reflexive pronoun used when the subject and the object of the verb are not the same entity
when: the subject is also the object of the verb

rules.quote: Don’t use reflexive pronouns such as ‘yourself’ and ‘myself’ as the subject of the verb.
rules.violation_condition: a reflexive pronoun used as the subject of a verb
rules.why: A clear structural constraint on reflexive pronouns.
